note: Compared with Cook's final ratings and the last public polls. Uncalled races can still shift as more votes are counted.

items.title: No tracked race called for a Republican
items.text: Of the 72 races on this page, 47 have been projected and all 47 went to Democrats, including 32 seats that flip from Republican control. 25 are still uncalled.

items.title: Texas flips both top races
items.text: AP projected Talarico (D) over Paxton (R) for Senate, 59.2%–39.2%, well above final polls (Talarico +3 to +7). AP also projected Hinojosa (D) over Gov. Abbott (R), after a final poll showing a 1-point race.

items.title: Senate toss-ups break one way
items.text: Democrats were projected to win Maine, Ohio, Kansas, Iowa and Michigan. AP called Michigan for El-Sayed (D) at 2:28 AM, 52.0%–46.0% with about 72% counted, a narrower margin than the 11-point final NYT/Siena poll.

items.title: NY-21 is the reversal of the night
items.text: Gendebien (D) led early, but with about 99% counted Constantino (R) leads 49%–47%, per WAMC, and has declared victory. No desk call yet.

items.title: Nevada governor flips overnight
items.text: AP projected Ford (D) over Gov. Lombardo (R) at 4:46 AM, 51.5%–44.3% with about 85% counted, in a race Cook rated a toss-up.

items.title: Still out
items.text: Alaska's Senate race is close and could go to ranked-choice tabulation on Nov. 18. Kansas governor is 50.3%–49.7%, FL-27 is headed to a recount, and ME-02, MI-04, MI-07 and NY-21 remain uncalled.
